title: Cairo Ministry Sit-In Dispersal
premise: Activists in Cairo clash with security forces after their weekly sit-in outside the Ministry of Finance is deemed illegal by a last-minute court order.

side_A.role: a researcher at a human-rights NGO
side_A.goal: documenting possible excessive force by police against protesters

side_B.goal: preparing criminal charges against protesters for rioting and property damage

=== DOCUMENT 1: Cairo Administrative Court - Case File 2024-5512: Order for Dispersal ===

**COURT RECORD**
**Case No:** 2024-5512
**Date:** Tuesday, 14 May 2024
**Time Issued:** 09:15
**Presiding Judge:** Judge H. Al-Sayed, Cairo Administrative Court

**ORDER:**

1.  **Context:** This Court reviews the status of the gathering at the Ministry of Finance, Cairo. The gathering commenced at 06:00 on 14 May 2024. At the time of this ruling, the assembly is ongoing.
2.  **Permit Status:** The organizers filed an application for a permit for this assembly 72 hours prior to the event. The application was reviewed and formally denied on Monday, 13 May 2024, at 16:00.
3.  **Ruling:** The Court declares the ongoing sit-in at the Ministry of Finance illegal. The assembly lacks legal standing due to the denial of the permit application.
4.  **Enforcement:** Security forces are authorized to enforce the dispersal of this illegal assembly. The objective is to enforce the court order to disperse the illegal assembly.
5.  **Service:** This order is to be served to the protest organizers immediately.

**Signed:**
H. Al-Sayed
Judge, Cairo Administrative Court

**Service Log:**
*   **Time:** 09:30
*   **Action:** Order served to protest organizers.
*   **Served By:** Bailiff M. Hassan
*   **Recipient:** Layla Hassan (Protest Organizer)

=== DOCUMENT 2: Ministry of Interior - Incident Log: Operation "Clear Plaza" ===

**INCIDENT LOG**
**Date:** 14 May 2024
**Location:** Public Plaza adjacent to Ministry of Finance (50 meters from main entrance)
**Unit:** Special Forces - Sector 4
**Commander:** Captain Rania Mostafa

**06:00**
Sit-in begins at the Ministry of Finance. Approximately 250 individuals present. The plaza is a public space with no physical barriers separating it from the street.

**09:15**
Court order issued declaring the sit-in illegal.

**09:30**
Court order served to organizers by bailiff.

**11:30**
Security forces arrive at the Ministry of Finance perimeter. Deployment consists of 40 officers equipped with riot gear.

**11:45**
Police announce a 30-minute dispersal deadline via loudspeaker. Announcement states that the illegal assembly must vacate the area within 30 minutes.

**11:50**
Police allow a designated spokesperson to approach the line for negotiation. Negotiation continues briefly.

**12:15**
Dispersal deadline expires. Confrontation begins. Protesters do not vacate the plaza.

**12:15 - 13:30**
Police utilize water cannons during the confrontation.
*   *Note from Cmdr. Mostafa:* "The first physical contact was initiated by protesters throwing rocks at the police line, prompting a defensive response. Tear gas was deployed only after protesters ignored three verbal warnings and began advancing on the police line."

**13:30**
Water cannon operation ceases.

**14:00**
Protesters vacate the plaza.

**Post-Incident Notes:**
*   Primary objective of the operation was to enforce the court order to disperse the illegal assembly.
*   12 individuals sustained injuries requiring hospitalization.
*   Medical records indicate injuries consistent with blunt force trauma and chemical exposure.
*   All arrests were of individuals who remained in the illegal assembly zone past the deadline, consistent with the court order.

=== DOCUMENT 3: Witness Statement of Layla Hassan ===

**STATEMENT OF WITNESS**
**Name:** Layla Hassan
**Role:** Protest Organizer
**Date:** 15 May 2024

I am a primary organizer of the sit-in at the Ministry of Finance. We filed for a permit 72 hours in advance, but the authorities denied our application on Monday evening at 16:00. Despite this, we maintained that we were exercising our right to peaceful assembly.

When the court order was served to us at 09:30 by the bailiff, we were aware of its existence. The sit-in had begun at 06:00, and by the time the order was issued at 09:15, we were still present. When security forces arrived at 11:30, there were approximately 250 of us in the plaza. The plaza is open, with no barriers, so the situation was visible to everyone.

At 11:45, the police announced a 30-minute dispersal deadline. We did not attempt to leave immediately because we believed we had the right to remain. We repeatedly requested to speak with police commanders to negotiate a peaceful exit, but were ignored.

At 12:15, when the deadline hit, the police did not wait. Tear gas was deployed directly into the crowd before any dispersal attempt, causing respiratory distress in non-combatants. It was indiscriminate. The police used water cannons from 12:15 until 13:30. It was a violent mob of officers who charged at us. We were forced to hold our ground until 14:00, when we finally vacated the plaza.

The injuries we sustained were severe. We saw people hit with batons while they were just sitting there. The police claimed they were responding to rocks, but that is a lie. We were peaceful. The arrests were made indiscriminately, including individuals who had already left the protest zone, without individualized charges. This was a crackdown, not law enforcement.

=== DOCUMENT 4: Witness Statement of Captain Rania Mostafa ===

**STATEMENT OF WITNESS**
**Name:** Captain Rania Mostafa
**Role:** Police Commander
**Date:** 15 May 2024

I commanded the 40 officers deployed at the Ministry of Finance on 14 May 2024. Our mandate was clear: enforce the court order issued at 09:15 by Judge H. Al-Sayed, which declared the sit-in illegal.

The sit-in began at 06:00. By 11:30, when we arrived, there were about 250 people. We established a perimeter. At 11:45, we issued a 30-minute dispersal deadline. We allowed a designated spokesperson to approach the line at 11:50 to discuss the situation. However, the negotiation ended when the crowd surged forward.

At 12:15, the deadline expired. The protesters did not vacate. The confrontation began. The first physical contact was initiated by protesters throwing rocks at the police line, prompting a defensive response. We did not attack a peaceful crowd; we responded to aggression.

We used water cannons between 12:15 and 13:30 to manage the crowd. Tear gas was deployed only after protesters ignored three verbal warnings and began advancing on the police line. It was a necessary measure to protect the safety of the officers and the public.

We continued to enforce the order until 14:00, when the protesters finally left. We arrested individuals who remained in the illegal assembly zone past the deadline. All arrests were consistent with the court order. We did not arrest anyone who had already left. The injuries reported are consistent with the chaotic nature of the confrontation, but our actions were proportional and defensive.

=== DOCUMENT 5: Medical Report - Cairo General Hospital, Trauma Ward ===

**MEDICAL REPORT**
**Date:** 14 May 2024
**Time:** 15:00
**Attending Physician:** Dr. Samir El-Ghazal, Medical Examiner
**Patients:** 12 individuals admitted from the Ministry of Finance plaza incident.

**Clinical Observations:**
Twelve patients were admitted following the incident at the public plaza adjacent to the Ministry of Finance. The injuries sustained by these individuals are consistent with blunt force trauma and chemical exposure.

**Specific Findings:**
1.  **Blunt Force Trauma:** Several patients present with contusions and lacerations on the upper back and head. The pattern of injury suggests strikes from a distance by a hard object.
    *   *Dr. El-Ghazal's Note:* "The first physical injuries were caused by police batons striking protesters who were seated peacefully. The victims were in a low posture, indicating they were not advancing on the police line at the time of impact."
2.  **Chemical Exposure:** All twelve patients exhibit signs of respiratory distress, corneal irritation, and chemical burns to the skin.
    *   *Dr. El-Ghazal's Note:* "The chemical agents used were consistent with tear gas. The distribution of symptoms suggests direct exposure to a concentrated cloud, rather than peripheral drift."

**Contextual Note:**
The medical timeline aligns with the police report of water cannon use between 12:15 and 13:30. However, the nature of the blunt force injuries contradicts the police claim of a "defensive response" to advancing protesters. The victims were stationary when struck.

**Conclusion:**
The injuries are severe and require hospitalization. The cause of the blunt force trauma is attributed to police batons used against seated individuals. The chemical exposure was direct and indiscriminate.

=== DOCUMENT 6: Witness Statement of Officer Karim Nour ===

**STATEMENT OF WITNESS**
**Name:** Officer Karim Nour
**Role:** Police Officer
**Date:** 15 May 2024

I was one of the 40 officers deployed at the Ministry of Finance on 14 May 2024. We arrived at 11:30. The plaza was full of people, about 250 of them. The police announced a 30-minute dispersal deadline at 11:45.

At 11:50, we let a spokesperson come forward. But then the crowd surged. At 12:15, when the deadline was up, the protesters started throwing rocks. The first physical contact was initiated by protesters throwing rocks at the police line, prompting a defensive response. We had to hold our ground.

Tear gas was deployed only after protesters ignored three verbal warnings and began advancing on the police line. It was not targeted at peaceful people; it was to stop the advance. We used water cannons from 12:15 to 13:30. The protesters did not leave until 14:00.

I saw people hit, but I also saw rocks coming at us. The injuries were consistent with the chaos. I did not see anyone being hit while sitting peacefully. The police were acting to enforce the court order. The arrests were of people who stayed in the illegal zone. We did not arrest people who left.

=== DOCUMENT 7: Witness Statement of Yusuf Amin ===

**STATEMENT OF WITNESS**
**Name:** Yusuf Amin
**Role:** Legal Advisor
**Date:** 15 May 2024

I was present at the Ministry of Finance plaza on 14 May 2024. The sit-in began at 06:00. The court order was issued at 09:15 and served at 09:30. The permit had been denied on Monday at 16:00.

When the police arrived at 11:30, there were about 250 people. The plaza is a public space with no barriers. The police announced a 30-minute deadline at 11:45. The organizers did not attempt to leave immediately.

At 12:15, the confrontation began. The police used water cannons until 13:30. The protesters did not vacate the plaza until 14:00.

I witnessed the arrests. Arrests were made indiscriminately, including individuals who had already left the protest zone, without individualized charges. The police claimed they only arrested those who stayed, but I saw people being taken away who were walking away from the center of the protest. The injuries were severe, consistent with blunt force and chemical exposure. The police used tear gas directly on the crowd. This was a violation of the right to peaceful assembly. The police commanders ignored requests to negotiate. The situation was controlled by the police, not by the protesters.
